findings.issue: Ten organizational identifiers are asserted as `ROR:` CURIEs (ROR:01yc7t268, ROR:00cvxb145, ROR:008s83205, ROR:0168r3w48, ROR:00za53h95, ROR:009avj582, ROR:00f54p054, ROR:0156zyn36, ROR:03r0ha626, ROR:03hamhx47). The bundle does supply ROR URLs for each of these organizations in the FAIRhub study description (sponsorCollaboratorsModule, overallOfficialList affiliations, locationList) and the FAIRhub dataset description managingOrganization, so the identifiers themselves are grounded and the CURIE form is correct. However, the bundle attaches these RORs to sponsor/collaborator/official affiliations of the study, not to the affiliations of the creator of record, which FAIRhub records as the single organizational creator "AI-READI Consortium". Attaching the full collaborator roster as affiliations of one Creator object over-reads the evidence; additionally the University of Utah (ROR:03r0ha626) and University of Massachusetts Lowell (ROR:03hamhx47) appear only as affiliations of individual overall officials (Contreras, Evans), never as project collaborators or data-collection institutions.

The slot is multivalued and the bundle names a distinct, enumerable Writing Committee, Principal Investigator list, staff list, project manager list and intern list (Nature Metabolism consortium author block), plus a single organizational creator (FAIRhub dataset description: creatorName 'AI-READI Consortium', nameType 'Organizational'). One Creator object carrying a PI plus ten affiliations plus explanatory notes collapses several distinct entities into one, contrary to the one-object-per-entity rule. At minimum the organizational creator recorded by the highest-ranked source is not represented as its own entity.

Source commentary is embedded in the Creator object rather than confined to `source_caveats`. The note explains that the creator of record is the AI-READI Consortium and that Lee is 'named study principal investigator and central contact' — that is an explanation of how the object was assembled, i.e. trust annotation about sibling slots, which the schema places in `source_caveats` (already present on the same object and already carrying a related remark).

`committee_name: AI-READI Data Access Committee` is a synthesized name. The BMJ Open protocol (tier 3) says 'The requirements for controlled access data sets are being currently developed by the Data Access Committee'; the RO-Crate (tier 1) records `dataGovernanceCommittee: "AI-READI Consortium"`. Neither source states the string 'AI-READI Data Access Committee'. The higher-ranked source gives 'AI-READI Consortium'; the constructed compound is unsupported.

Aaron Y. Lee (ORCID:0000-0002-7452-1648) is placed as the governance committee contact. The bundle supports him as study PI, responsible party, and central study contact (centralContactEMail contact@aireadi.org), but nowhere designates him as contact for the access/governance committee. The RO-Crate names the governance committee only as 'AI-READI Consortium' with no contact person; the license names the licensor as Washington University in St. Louis. This is an inference, not an attested value.

`RO_CRATE` is included in the dataset-level list. The bundle shows an RO-Crate metadata file describing the dataset (ro-crate-metadata.json, conformsTo https://w3id.org/ro/crate/1.2-DRAFT), which is a property of a packaging/metadata artifact about the dataset rather than a standard the dataset's own content follows. The dataset-level `conforms_to` value names only CDS; the data-type standards are DICOM, OMOP CDM, WFDB, Open mHealth and the NASA ASCII/ESDS guidelines. Listing RO_CRATE alongside them conflates a metadata-packaging profile with content standards.

`ark:59853/rocrate-b2ai-aireadi-release-3-0-0#root-metadata` is a minted fragment for a 'Root metadata files' collection that no other value in the record points at. Under the minting rule, a fragment identifier is warranted only where another value must reference the part; a part that is merely described should be described in prose. No slot references this collection.

`file_count: 9` is computed by counting the nine entries in the FAIRhub `metadataFileList` (CHANGELOG.md, dataset_description.json, dataset_structure_description.json, healthsheet.md, LICENSE.txt, participants.json, participants.tsv, README.md, study_description.json). The bundle lists those files but never states a count, and never states that these nine constitute a file collection with that cardinality. The derived integer is an unsupported quantitative claim.

`B2AI_TOPIC:43` (Diabetes) is asserted as the single topic for an instance the record itself describes as spanning survey, clinical, retinal imaging, ECG, environmental, CGM and wearable activity data. Selecting one topic term is defensible, but the instance is a participant, and the enumerated substrate slot (`data_substrate`) that would carry the heterogeneous data forms is omitted while the topic is narrowed to the disease. Either the choice should be justified in `source_caveats` or the slot omitted, since the bundle supplies no topic classification for instances.

`publisher: https://fairhub.io/` is a resolver URL in a slot whose declared range is `uriorcurie`. The bundle states the publisherName as 'FAIRhub' (FAIRhub dataset description, `publisher.publisherName`). No declared prefix covers FAIRhub, so a URL is the permitted fallback — but the trailing-slash landing-page URL is also the value used in `page` for a different resource (https://fairhub.io/datasets/3), and using the bare platform URL as an identifier for the publishing organization is weaker than the plain name the source gives.

Four DatasetRelationship entries use `is_new_version_of` (twice) and `is_described_by` (twice). The two version relationships are supported by the FAIRhub versions list. The two `is_described_by` entries point at doi:10.1038/s42255-024-01165-x and doi:10.1136/bmjopen-2024-097449; the RO-Crate records these as `associatedPublication` and the FAIRhub relatedIdentifier block records `IsDocumentedBy` only for https://docs.aireadi.org/ and https://aireadi.org/. No source states an IsDescribedBy relation to either publication, so the relationship type is inferred rather than attested.

The ClinicalTrials.gov entry carries a `source_caveats` that characterizes the BMJ Open citation ('Clinicaltrials.org approval number STUDY00016228') as the IRB protocol number 'rather than a trial registration'. Identifying STUDY00016228 as the UW IRB number is supported elsewhere in the bundle, but the judgment that the BMJ citation is therefore an error is the record's own inference about a source's mistake, not a transcription of source conflict.

The value merges two source statements into one causal narrative: FAIRhub's 'No identifiers were collected so no active de-identification was necessary but we checked that no identifiable data per US HIPAA were present' and Nature Metabolism's 'The public set is stripped of Protected Health Information (PHI) ... via the "Safe Harbor" method'. These are in tension — one says no de-identification was performed, the other says PHI was stripped by a named method. The `source_caveats` on the same object does flag the tension, but `method` asserts both as a single procedure.

`is_representative: false` is asserted. The bundle supports non-representativeness by design (deliberate equal-proportion balancing rather than mirroring the US population; healthsheet limitations on urban/hospital-based recruitment and missing Pacific Islander and Native American groups), so the value is defensible — but no source states a representativeness determination in these terms, and the healthsheet answers the corresponding question with 'The dataset contains all possible instances', which does not address representativeness. The boolean is an interpretation.

`hipaa_compliant: compliant` is an enum determination the bundle does not make. Sources state that the release contains no PHI, that FAIRhub's deIdentHIPAA flag is true, and that results were returned to participants by 'HIPAA-compliant, encrypted email' — none of which is a compliance status assertion for the dataset. The permitted value `not_applicable` may be closer given the record's own claim that no PHI is present; either way the chosen term is inferred.

`was_inferred_derived: false` is asserted, but the record elsewhere documents derived values: BMI and waist-hip ratio are calculated (`variables`), log CS is computed from errors and the final correct letter (`variables[.].derivation`), and OCTA segmentation heightmaps are device-derived products. The healthsheet answer the value is drawn from addresses only directly-observed versus subject-reported acquisition and does not deny derivation, so the explicit `false` contradicts the record's own variable-level statements.

`3815969779678` is taken from the FAIRhub API `data.size` field and is supported. Note for consistency only: the sum of the nine subcrate `total_bytes` values recorded in `file_collections` is approximately 3.816 TB and does not include the root metadata collection, for which no `total_bytes` is given — so the aggregate and the parts are consistent in magnitude but the record does not state that the total is the API figure rather than a sum. A `source_caveats` noting the provenance of the total would remove the ambiguity.

The value quotes the RO-Crate's organization name 'Washington University IRB' while simultaneously reciting a University of Washington Human Subjects Division postal address, presenting the conflict inline in the slot value rather than in `source_caveats`. The parallel `ethical_reviews[0]` object handles the same conflict correctly by placing it in `source_caveats`; the two treatments are inconsistent.

Omission. The healthsheet maintenance section asks 'Is there an erratum?' and the response is empty, which is an absence of information rather than an assertion of none. Correctly omitted here; flagged only to confirm the omission is deliberate and that no erratum content in the bundle was overlooked.

Omission that the bundle arguably supports as an explicit negative: the healthsheet uses section asks 'Has the dataset been used for any tasks already?' and answers 'No'. The schema's ExistingUse class has no boolean to carry a negative, so omission is defensible, but the explicit 'No' is evidence the record does not surface anywhere.

Omission that the bundle supports as an explicit negative: the healthsheet asks whether there is a repository linking papers or systems that use the dataset and answers 'No'. As with `existing_uses`, the class offers no negative-carrying field, so omission is defensible; noted for completeness.

All four are omitted. This is correct — the healthsheet labeling section answers 'N/A - no labels are provided' repeatedly, states 'no labeling was performed', and the RO-Crate records `rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: "N/A - no labels are provided"`; no imputation is described anywhere. Flagged only to confirm the omissions are evidence-backed rather than oversights.

Omitted, correctly: the bundle names no compression format for the release. Confirmed against the FAIRhub `format` list (application/dicom, text/markdown, text/csv, application/json), which contains no archive or compression media type.

summary: Audited the full record against the declared bundle. The record is broadly well-grounded: participant counts, file counts, byte sizes, per-subcrate breakdowns, dates, license terms, consent and IRB details, device inventory, split table and standards mapping all trace to attested passages, and the three declared source conflicts (institutional attribution, target enrollment, collection start date) are resolved in favour of the higher-ranked source with the alternative recorded, as required. No fabricated dataset facts were found and no prior-D4D contamination is evident. The defects concentrate in three areas. First, the `creators` slot: a single Creator object carries a PI, ten institutional ROR affiliations drawn from the study's sponsor/collaborator/official rosters rather than from any statement about dataset authorship, and explanatory commentary in `notes` that belongs in `source_caveats`; the organizational creator of record ('AI-READI Consortium', the only creator FAIRhub names) is not represented as its own entity, and two of the ten RORs attach only to individual officials. Second, `data_governance`: both `committee_name` ('AI-READI Data Access Committee') and `committee_contact` (Aaron Y. Lee) are constructed rather than transcribed — the RO-Crate gives 'AI-READI Consortium' with no contact, and the BMJ protocol mentions only an unnamed 'Data Access Committee'. Third, several enum and boolean determinations are the record's own interpretations rather than source statements: `hipaa_compliant: compliant`, `sampling_strategies[0].is_representative: false`, `acquisition_methods[0].was_inferred_derived: false` (which contradicts the record's own documented derived variables), and the inclusion of `RO_CRATE` in `conforms_to_standard`, which conflates a metadata-packaging profile with the content standards the dataset follows. Two lower-severity structural issues: a minted fragment identifier for a root-metadata file collection that nothing in the record references, contrary to the minting rule, and a `file_count: 9` for that collection derived by counting list entries the bundle never totals. Remaining findings are minor placement issues — source commentary inline in `human_subject_research.ethics_review_board` and in an `external_resources` caveat where a sibling object handles the same conflict correctly — plus confirmations that several omissions (errata, existing_uses, use_repository, labeling and imputation slots, compression) are evidence-backed rather than oversights. No shape violations against the schema digest were found: all multivalued slots carry lists, all enum values are drawn from the permitted sets, all `uriorcurie` slots use CURIEs where a prefix is declared, `access_urls` correctly carries URLs in a `uri`-ranged slot, the `doi` slot carries the bare anchored form, and both datetime slots carry UTC offsets.
